steps.caption: Two arrows on the axes: u = (1, 0) and w = (0, 1). The matrix A will act on every vector.
Apply A. Each arrow moves to A times itself. Watch where each ends up, and whether it still lies on its original line (the dashed ghost).
u went from (1, 0) to (2, 0). Same line, twice as long. So u is an eigenvector of A, and the stretch factor 2 is its eigenvalue.
w went from (0, 1) to (1, 3). It left its line: it was turned as well as stretched. So w is not an eigenvector.

set.text: A w  is not a multiple of w

steps.caption: Eigenvector: a nonzero v with A v = lambda v. A only stretches it (a negative lambda flips it). To find them, solve det(A - lambda I) = 0.
Try a third arrow, z = (1, 1), on the diagonal.
z lands at (3, 3), still on its own line, three times longer. A second eigenvector, with eigenvalue 3. Here det(A - lambda I) = (2 - lambda)(3 - lambda), giving lambda = 2 and 3.
